PART 03

Grammar · Frequency Adverbs & Expressions

How often do you do something?

We use frequency adverbs with the present simple to talk about routines and how often we do things.

FrequencyAdverbExample
100%alwaysI always watch TV on the weekend.
≈80%usuallyI usually read the newspaper.
≈60%oftenI often go for a walk.
≈40%sometimesI sometimes study English.
≈10%hardly everI hardly ever drink coffee.
0%neverI never watch soccer.
✅ Before a main verb: I always listen to the radio.
✅ After be: They are never late.

Frequency expressions

Use every, once, twice, three times to talk about regular habits.

ExpressionExample
every dayI see my parents every day.
once a weekI visit my grandparents once a week.
twice a monthWe go to the movies twice a month.
three times a yearI see my cousins three times a year.
Position: frequency expressions usually go at the end of a sentence.
Once = one time   ·   Twice = two times
How often do you visit your family?

PART 05

Reading · Family get-togethers

Before you read · Pair discussion

1. When and where do you spend time with your family? Tell your partner.

2. Look at the pictures. How many generations can you see? What are they doing together?

Example: I see my family on the weekend. We have lunch together on Sundays.

PART 06

Speaking · Time Together

Task 1 · Talk to your partner

Work in pairs and ask these questions, using vocabulary and frequency expressions from this lesson.

01

How often do you spend time with your family?

02

What do you usually do when you get together?

03

Do you often see your grandparents or cousins?

04

Who usually cooks at your family get-togethers?

A: How often do you spend time with your family?
B: I usually have dinner with my parents every day, but I only see my grandparents once a month.
A: What do you do when you get together?
B: We often cook together, talk, and sometimes play games.

Task 2 · Mini speaking project

Prepare a 60–90 second talk about a family get-together you enjoy.

Speaking plan: Who is there? · Where do you meet? · How often? · What do you do together? · Why is it special?
My family usually gets together on Sunday evenings. We meet at my grandparents’ house, and there are often three generations there. My parents and my aunt usually cook dinner, while my cousins and I sometimes play board games. We hardly ever watch TV because we prefer talking. I really enjoy these evenings because we can catch up and spend quality time together.
